set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

evidence_timeline.summary: Following the detection of the sub-solar mass merger candidate S251112cm (the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42650), we conducted follow-up observations focused on the northern region of the initial bayestar skymap (GCN 42650) using the newly deployed 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST Collaboration; Wang et al., 2023) at the Lenghu Astronomical Observation Base (Qinghai province, China). Observations began at UTC 2025-11-13T11:29:36, corresponding to ~20.2 hours after the merger event (UTC 2025-11-12T15:18:45). The follow-ups lasted for three nights until UTC 2025-11-15T23:16:16. We observed in WFST g, r, and i bands with exposure times of 45-90 seconds. A total area of about 727.4 square degrees of the 90% skymap (GCN 42650) was observed, covering ~64% of the event localization. Additionally, ~7.5% skymap was covered in 30s g- and r-band exposures through the WFST wide-field survey (WFS) 6.35 hours after the merger event. The follow-up observation data were processed using the WFST pipeline. For images localized in WFS, image subtraction was performed using the WFST stacking images taken berfore the event as templates. The search for the counterpart of S251112cm was performed mainly through visual inspection based on the locations of nearby galaxies, considering the distance estimate of 93 +/- 27 Mpc (redshift ~ 0.02; the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42690) and the uncertainty of the potential electromagnetic counterpart. All extragalactic transient candidates detected by WFST during follow-ups were reported to the IAU Transient Name Server (TNS). After excluding sources with pre-merger detections reported in TNS, only one candidate was found to be located near a galaxy with spectroscopic redshift below 0.045: AT2025aebp was first detected at 60992.93 (+1.3 days post-merger) with 21.5 +/- 0.1 mag in r-band, and the spectroscopic redshift of its possible host galaxy SDSS J103703.20+231142.2 is 0.043. Additionally, we report three other sources without pre-merger detections. publication_revisions.abstract: Following the detection of the sub-solar mass merger candidate S251112cm (the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42650), we conducted follow-up observations focused on the northern region of the initial bayestar skymap (GCN 42650) using the newly deployed 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST Collaboration; Wang et al., 2023) at the Lenghu Astronomical Observation Base (Qinghai province, China). Observations began at UTC 2025-11-13T11:29:36, corresponding to ~20.2 hours after the merger event (UTC 2025-11-12T15:18:45). The follow-ups lasted for three nights until UTC 2025-11-15T23:16:16. We observed in WFST g, r, and i bands with exposure times of 45-90 seconds. A total area of about 727.4 square degrees of the 90% skymap (GCN 42650) was observed, covering ~64% of the event localization. Additionally, ~7.5% skymap was covered in 30s g- and r-band exposures through the WFST wide-field survey (WFS) 6.35 hours after the merger event. The follow-up observation data were processed using the WFST pipeline. For images localized in WFS, image subtraction was performed using the WFST stacking images taken berfore the event as templates. The search for the counterpart of S251112cm was performed mainly through visual inspection based on the locations of nearby galaxies, considering the distance estimate of 93 +/- 27 Mpc (redshift ~ 0.02; the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra Collaboration, GCN 42690) and the uncertainty of the potential electromagnetic counterpart.
